THE MODEL DOES NOT COMPUTE SHARES AND AMOUNTS: articles 8.5, 11.1.9–11.1.13 and 11.2.4 name the rule (to the extent of the lesser obligation, in equal shares, proportionally), while the numbers are brought by the case. Proportional imputation of a set-off (article 8.4(2)) is declared rather than computed for the same reason.
- **Does not answer:** Which circumstances indicate that the obligations are separate? — data the case must bring (PICC_ART11_1_2_EN). SOLIDARITY IS PRESUMED (article 11.1.2), AND THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE REBUT IT. The source does not enumerate which circumstances indicate separate obligations — that is an assertion of the case.

Where the obligations are to pay money in different currencies, set-off may be exercised provided that both currencies are freely convertible and no single currency was agreed (`ForeignCurrencySetOff`); Article 8.1(1). Where two parties owe each other performances of the same kind, either may set off if it is entitled to perform its own obligation and the other party's obligation is ascertained and due (`SetOffConditions`); Article 8.1(2). THE 1980 UN CONVENTION HAS NEITHER SET-OFF NOR ASSIGNMENT NOR SOLIDARITY AT ALL: its subject is the formation of a contract for the international sale of goods and the rights of the parties under it. There is no bridge to `intl.uncitral.cisg*` here in substance, not for want of work; the way to these chapters is opened by article 7(2) of the Convention.
- **Does not answer:** Is the obligation of an exclusively personal character and does the assignment make it more burdensome? — data the case must bring (PICC_ART9_1_3_EN, PICC_ART9_1_7_EN). AN EXCLUSIVELY PERSONAL CHARACTER OF AN OBLIGATION (articles 9.1.7, 9.2.6) AND A SIGNIFICANTLY MORE BURDENSOME OBLIGATION CAUSED BY AN ASSIGNMENT (articles 9.1.3, 9.1.4) ARE FACTS OF THE CASE: both assessments are brought by the case, not derived by the model.
